correctness.summary: The annular interpolation proof is correct. With a_m=2m+2n and u=log r, the radial moment exponent F_m(u)=a_m u-u^(3/2) has its unique maximum at u_m=4a_m^2/9. The proposed m-th annulus has logarithmic endpoints 4(a_m-1)^2/9 and 4(a_m+1)^2/9, and direct substitution gives exponent drops -4(3a_m-2)/27 and -4(3a_m+2)/27. Hence both normalized tails tend exponentially to zero (up to harmless polynomial factors). A symbol equal to c_m on that annulus therefore has Toeplitz eigenvalue lambda_m=c_m+o(1) for every bounded sequence c. Since each homogeneous P^m block is finite dimensional, the diagonal difference is compact exactly when its scalar block values tend to zero. The multiplicity-free U(n) decomposition then identifies the full diagonal commutant quotient with l-infinity/c0, so surjectivity of the radial Toeplitz Calkin image follows.

limitations: The theorem is specific to the displayed logarithmic radial weight and bounded radial symbols.
It identifies the algebra only modulo compact operators, not an operator-norm equality with the full intertwiner algebra.
The motivating preprint is extremely recent and the interpolation amplification is elementary once its concentration estimates are known.

originality.summary: Bdarneh's September 2026 preprint supplies the radial eigenvalue formula and, for the same logarithmic weight, constructs a bounded radial symbol whose eigenvalue sequence violates square-root uniform continuity. Its public statement does not claim arbitrary bounded-sequence interpolation or identify the complete Calkin image. Searches did not locate the full l-infinity/c0 corona theorem elsewhere. The new step is nevertheless a short amplification of Bdarneh's concentration mechanism, so priority and depth are appropriately described as a structural corollary/refinement rather than an unrelated new theory.

scientific_value.summary: Upgrading one non-uniformly-continuous witness to arbitrary bounded diagonal data determines the entire radial Toeplitz algebra modulo compacts and exposes a sharp contrast with the Gaussian square-root-uniform corona. The result is strong at the quotient level even though it is specific to one logarithmic weight.
